stops.name: Parco naturale regionale di Porto Conte
stops.detail: Porto Conte Regional Natural Park (also officially in Algherese Catalan: Parc natural regional de Port del Comte e in sardo: Parcu natural regional de Portu Conte) is a protected natural area of the Coral Riviera located in north-western Sardinia north of Alghero. It takes its name from the site of considerable geo/naturalistic importance of Porto Conte in which it insists for great territorial prevalence. It was established by Regional Law No. 4 of 26 February 1999. It occupies an area of 5,350 it has in the administrative territory of the municipality of Alghero, to which the constitution, which took place in the same year, of the management body of the park, the Special Company Parco di Porto Conte.
